transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because... we recently put in this new, brighter mirror in our bathroom, and ever since then, I just keep noticing my face. Specifically, the skin around my cheeks and my jaw. 

It just looks really uneven to me, or kind of saggy. My husband says he can't really see what I'm talking about when I point it out, but I just keep seeing it, and it's been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
How much time each day do you find yourself thinking about the skin on your cheeks and jaw?

I'm not exactly sure. I haven't really timed it or anything. 

It's not like I'm sitting there for hours at a time, especially since I'm pretty busy at the law firm during the day. But... I guess it just pops into my head a few times a day. Mostly when I'm getting ready in the morning, or if I happen to use the restroom and see a mirror. I'll stop and look at my jawline for a few minutes, maybe pull at the skin a little. 

So, I don't have an exact amount of time for you. It's just happening often enough that it's getting frustrating.
Do you find yourself checking your cheeks or jaw in mirrors over and over?

Well, yeah, I suppose I do check it. Most mornings, I end up checking my face from a few different angles in that new mirror. I usually end up putting on a little extra makeup to try and smooth it out before I head to the courthouse for work. 

And, you know, sometimes during the day I find myself comparing my face to the other women I see at the firm. Or... if someone wants to take a casual picture at an office birthday or something, I'll kind of step out of the frame or avoid it if I'm not feeling okay about how my jaw looks that day. But it's mostly just checking in the morning and maybe touching up my makeup.
How much is this bothering you emotionally?

I mean, it's annoying, for sure. It bothers me enough that I'm here talking to you about it. But... it's not ruining my life or anything. It's just frustrating. I get a little down about it when I'm looking in the mirror, but once I get to work and get busy with cases, I can usually push it out of my mind. It's just a low-level annoyance most days.
Has worrying about your cheeks or jaw caused problems in your daily life?

Well, I still get all my work done at the firm, so it hasn't caused any major issues there. But... the extra time I spend checking the mirror and doing my makeup in the morning has definitely made me rush into the courthouse a few times. 

And it's made me late for my evening yoga class more than once, just from taking too long to get ready or fixing things. Outside of work, I've skipped being in a few casual photos at my book club and some community events. I just didn't want to deal with worrying about how my jaw or cheeks were going to look in the pictures. So, it's getting in the way a little bit, but mostly just making me run late and avoid cameras.
When other people look at your cheeks or jaw, do they usually seem to notice the problem the way you do?

Well, no, not really. Like I mentioned, I really started noticing it after we put in this new, brighter bathroom mirror. To me, the skin around my cheeks and jaw just looks uneven, or maybe kind of saggy. But my husband, he says he can't really see what I'm talking about. So I guess other people don't notice it the same way I do.
Besides looking in the mirror, do you find yourself doing other repeated things because of your cheeks or jaw, like touching them, comparing them, or trying to hide them?

Yeah, I do a few of those things. Like I said, most mornings I end up checking my face from a few different angles in the mirror, just to see how it looks. And I usually put on a little extra makeup before I head out to the courthouse, trying to even things out. 

I also catch myself comparing my face to other women I see at work, just wondering if they have the same issue. And, like I mentioned before, I'll avoid being in casual pictures if I'm not feeling okay about how my jaw or cheeks look that day. But I don't really sit there touching my face all day or anything like that.
Would you say this concern about your cheeks and jaw causes you a lot of distress?

Well, no, I wouldn't say it causes me a lot of distress. I mean, it's definitely frustrating, and I don't like how it looks, but... I'm not crying over it or letting it ruin my day. It's really just more of an annoyance that bugs me when I'm getting ready or if someone pulls out a camera. It doesn't upset me on a deep level or anything like that.
On a typical day, about how much total time do you spend thinking about or checking your cheeks and jaw?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I've never timed it or anything. I mean, it's mostly just when I'm getting ready in the morning, putting on my makeup before work. And maybe if I go to the restroom at the office, I might glance at it in the mirror. But I'm definitely not spending hours thinking about it or anything like that. It's just... I don't know, a little bit of time here and there.
Are these worries mostly just about how your cheeks and jaw look?

Yeah, it's pretty much just my cheeks and jaw. I mean, I don't love everything about getting older, but my face shape is really the only thing that actually bothers me. I don't sit around worrying about my weight or my hair or anything like that. It's just the cheeks and the jawline.
Aside from your concerns about your cheeks and jaw, have you been feeling depressed most days lately?
No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling depressed. I mean, my mood is generally fine. I go to work, I do what I need to do... I'm not feeling down or sad most days. Just normal, I guess.
On a typical day, do thoughts about your cheeks or jaw take up more than an hour total?

No, I really don't think it adds up to a full hour. Like I said, it's mostly just when I'm getting ready. Honestly, the main reason it's been on my mind so much lately is because we recently put in a brighter bathroom mirror at home. Ever since we did that, I just keep noticing that the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven, or kind of saggy to me. I see it every time I'm in front of that mirror, even though my husband says he can't really see what I'm talking about. So it's not taking up my whole day, it's just really noticeable to me when I'm in there.
Outside of your cheeks and jaw, do you tend to worry a lot about many other parts of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I have the usual stress, like anyone else. Work can be busy, bills have to be paid, that kind of thing. But I wouldn't say I'm a worrier in general. It's really just the stuff with my face that bothers me. Everything else is pretty manageable.
